text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000129's 99215 rate is far above what its patient complexity predicts and is concentrated on low-complexity patients, but the few documented 99215 charts support the billed level.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims data point toward upcoding: the excess 99215 share holds within every complexity stratum, and most sampled 99215s are for 0–1 condition patients with simple diagnoses such as R21, N39.0 or M54.50 (for example C0081178 and C0081192). Against that, none of the documented 99215 charts was coded below the billed level. C0080995, a single-condition osteoarthritis visit, was documented at high MDM with 45 minutes, as was the complex visit C0081291. Only 10 of 59 99215 claims have records, though, so the documentation is too thin to clear the pattern. The note signals also leave room for notes inflated to match the billing: the problems flag on about half of notes (e.g., C0080993, a 99215 with Z09 only), repeated visit times, and two moderate-plus data claims with no lab line on the claim. As a first step, request charts for more of the low-complexity 99215 claims and review the problems-flagged notes, checking whether the documented MDM and minutes plausibly fit what are mostly follow-up or minor-complaint diagnoses."}
